premise: I emptied my $98,000 nursing pension to co‑found a medical alert pendant company with my brother‑in‑law, notarizing 50/50 and a promise of free monitoring for my senior‑exercise group; when a telehealth conglomerate offered $550,000 for the subscriber base, he forged a dissolution, sold the assets, and sent me a $3,900 “monitoring” check—I found the original contract hidden behind the faceplate of a prototype pendant, voided the sale, and now run “Pendant of Perjury Alerts,” where he assembles wristbands in a smock that says “Fall Detection of Lies” and every device box prints his fraud docket number.
